chunks.content: # CLO Beginner's Tutorial: Simulation Control and Optimization Form This document explains simulation control and shape optimization tools in CLO, focusing on fixed needles, sewing tools, range drag, and fabric hardening versus shape solidification. It includes detailed workflows, tool usage, and tips for improving simulation speed and garment fitting. --- ## Simulation Speed Optimization and Using Fixed Needles This section covers techniques to enhance simulation speed by freezing garment pieces and using fixed needles to control garment position during simulation. - **Freezing Garments**: To speed up simulation, freeze garment pieces that contact the scarf, such as the collar and front/back panels, by right-clicking and selecting freeze. Use shortcut Ctrl+Shift+I to toggle freeze on selected pieces. Press Shift to select the scarf piece separately. - **Anti-Aggression Plate and Sewing Line**: Setting these on other pieces further reduces calculation load. - **Adding Fixed Needles**: Fixed needles prevent garments like scarves from falling during simulation. - Access the Fixed Needle tool by long-pressing the third tool in the left toolbar. - Choose between the Fixed Needle Case tool and Fixed Needle Set tool; both add fixed needles differently. - Adding fixed needles is done by selecting a grid frame in 2D or 3D panels; a red dot indicates the fixed needle's position. - Selected fixed needles appear orange in 3D; unselected ones are red. - Multiple fixed needles can be added to a set by pressing Ctrl+Shift while selecting. - To delete fixed needles: select with Ctrl in 2D or right-click and delete in 3D. - Double-clicking a line adds a row of fixed needles quickly. - **Positioning Fixed Needles on the Scarf**: - Add two rows of fixed needles along the scarf edges and two rows in the middle front area. - If mistakenly selecting back grids, use Ctrl to deselect unnecessary fixed needles. - Move fixed needles using the Move tool during simulation. - When moving fixed needles while simulation is paused, only the selected grids move; in active simulation, connected grids move together. - **Adjusting Fixed Needle Position**: - Use the Shift key to select fixed needles in 3D. - Move the positioning balls to adjust the fixed needles so they pass smoothly through the scarf ring. - Rotate the view with Shift to check alignment from different angles. - Avoid pulling fixed needles too tight to maintain natural scarf fit. - The left side requires rotation from bottom to outside, then inside the scarf circle, ensuring smooth passage. - Pause simulation frequently during fixed needle adjustments to record shape and avoid resetting. - **Tightening the Scarf**: - After fitting, select fixed needles at both scarf ends with Shift. - Move them closer to the model using positioning balls to tighten. - Delete temporary fixed needles by right-click or Ctrl+W after adjustment. - **Refining Simulation Parameters**: - Reduce scarf particle diameter to 10 mm and thickness to 1 mm for more realistic simulation. - Simulate again to observe enhanced fabric behavior.

Gradually advance to mastering garment production techniques.

chunks.content: - Pause simulation frequently during fixed needle adjustments to record shape and avoid resetting. - **Tightening the Scarf**: - After fitting, select fixed needles at both scarf ends with Shift. - Move them closer to the model using positioning balls to tighten. - Delete temporary fixed needles by right-click or Ctrl+W after adjustment. - **Refining Simulation Parameters**: - Reduce scarf particle diameter to 10 mm and thickness to 1 mm for more realistic simulation. - Simulate again to observe enhanced fabric behavior. --- ## Adding Single-Point Fixed Needles in 3D and Adjusting Shape This section explains how to add single-point fixed needles directly on the 3D garment and use them to modify garment shape during simulation. - While pressing **W**, right-click on the desired 3D garment location and select "Add Single-Point Fixed Needle". - The fixed needle can be moved with positioning balls. - Start simulation and drag the fixed needle point to adjust garment shape dynamically. - To delete a single-point fixed needle, right-click on it or press **W** and right-click again. --- ## Using the Sewing Tool to Adjust Garment Shape This section describes how to use the sewing tool to connect and manipulate garment points to optimize shape and fit. - Select the **Sewing Tool**. - Click two points on either 2D or 3D panels to connect them with a blue sewing line. - Switch to **Edit Sewing Tool** to adjust the connection points or line length. - When simulation is on, connected points are fixed together, influencing garment shape. - Use the sewing tool to pull or adjust distances on parts of the scarf, e.g., right side shaping. - Default sewing line length is 0 mm; change length (e.g., 30–50 mm) in the right-hand attribute editor to fine-tune fit. - Multiple sewing lines (1–2 sets) can be added for better control. - Reducing scarf particle diameter further to 5 mm enhances simulation realism. - After sewing adjustments, activate all sweater and skirt pieces (select all, right-click Activate) and simulate for natural integration. --- ## Range Drag Tool for Complex Shape Manipulation This section explains the use of the range drag tool for manipulating garment grids over an area, useful for correcting twisted or intersecting panels. - Open the practice file with a twisted strap example. - Instead of manually pulling grids, use the **Range Drag Tool** for smoother control. - Enable simulation. - Select the move tool, long-press to switch to **Range Drag** mode (mouse pointer changes to two concentric circles). - Inner circle defines core selection; outer circle defines falloff range. - Adjust display weight in the right panel for visualizing selection. - Drag selected green-highlighted area in 3D by left-click and dragging. - Adjust soft selection range and drag force via reduction settings. - Modes: - **Surface mode**: drag effect applies only on the selected surface area. - **Straight line mode**: selects all panels within a range (e.g., 10 points). - Use side view for precise dragging.

chunks.content: - Inner circle defines core selection; outer circle defines falloff range. - Adjust display weight in the right panel for visualizing selection. - Drag selected green-highlighted area in 3D by left-click and dragging. - Adjust soft selection range and drag force via reduction settings. - Modes: - **Surface mode**: drag effect applies only on the selected surface area. - **Straight line mode**: selects all panels within a range (e.g., 10 points). - Use side view for precise dragging. - After manipulation, remove fixed pins and re-simulate. - Switch back to normal move tool by long-pressing again. --- ## Hardening vs. Shape Solidification: Fabric Behavior Control This section contrasts the **Hardening** and **Shape Solidification** features in CLO, used to control fabric wrinkle and shape during simulation. - Open the practice file with two T-shirts. ### Hardening (Shortcut: Ctrl+H) - Select a garment (double-click), right-click and choose **Hardening**. - The garment turns orange, and wrinkles flatten. - Material becomes temporarily rubber-like and stiff. - Used for flattening fabric or dealing with severe curls. - Right-click again and remove hardening to restore softness. ### Shape Solidification (Shortcut: Ctrl+E) - Select a garment, right-click and choose **Shape Solidification**. - Wrinkles and original shape are preserved. - During simulation, the garment moves as a whole without shape change. - Solidified garments maintain their form but remain physically simulated and movable. - Ideal for fixing a specific style or wrinkle pattern. **Use cases**: - Hardening is for flattening or removing wrinkles. - Shape solidification maintains detailed garment shape while allowing movement. --- # Summary This tutorial demonstrates key CLO tools for garment simulation control and optimization, including: - Speeding up simulation via freezing and anti-aggression plate settings. - Adding and positioning fixed needles for garment stability. - Using sewing tools to modify shape and fit with adjustable sewing lines. - Applying range drag for complex grid manipulation. - Differentiating between hardening and shape solidification to control fabric wrinkle and form. These methods ensure more precise, realistic garment simulations and efficient workflow in CLO.
